mike_support: FYI AcmePay (acct: acme-242) opened a high-sev ticket. Their integration started failing after we enabled structured output strict enforcement. Client sees JSON parse errors. They claim we returned HTML with a 200 which breaks their parser. olivia_engineer: Can you paste the raw response + headers they got? Also need the api key + request id so we can grep logs (redact key in chat). mike_support: Pasted the snippet they sent (redacted): -- request info -- endpoint: POST /v1/generate headers: Authorization: Bearer REDACTED Content-Type: application/json Accept: application/json X-Client-Name: acmepay-integ payload: {"prompt":"...","response_format":"json","json_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"string"}}}} response headers: HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8 Content-Length: 2543 X-Request-ID: req_abc123 response body (first lines): Service Unavailable

Temporarily offline for maintenance

... mike_support: Customer says their client immediately throws JSON.parse error and they can't fall back; they rely on strict JSON enforcement. They switched to response_format=json recently and it used to work. olivia_engineer: Interesting. We should not be returning an HTML maintenance page for API requests. That suggests an intermediary (WAF/load balancer) or our error handler returned an HTML page for a non-JSON route. I will check service logs for X-Request-ID req_abc123. raj_sre: I see a deploy yesterday that added an HTML maintenance banner for traffic routed to a deprecated gateway. deploy-bot? deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-09T21:12Z by infra-release: merged "gateway: add maintenance banner middleware" (rev: a1b2c3). Canary to gateway-v2. raj_sre: That middleware returns a 200 HTML page under certain header patterns (missing X-API-GATEWAY: true). Seems our gateway rejects unknown client headers and returns an HTML notice. Should have returned 503 with JSON error. olivia_engineer: Repro steps I ran from my laptop (curl): curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -d '{"prompt":"test","response_format":"json","strict":true}' Result: 200 OK, Content-Type: text/html; body contains maintenance page. The gateway logged: gateway: banner middleware triggered for header X-Client-Name=acmepay-integ (policy: unknown). olivia_engineer: Also saw our runtime validation rejecting the HTML earlier: structured-output validator raised "Invalid JSON response: unexpected token '<' at position 0" and returned an internal parse error upstream but the gateway swallowed it. lisa_support_mgr: Priority: high. Customer is in prod and parsing errors are preventing payments. Need quick mitigation + long-term fix. mike_support: Customer requests: 1) explanation 2) mitigation (workaround) 3) ETA for fix. They can add header if we tell them which one. raj_sre: Immediate mitigation: instruct customer to set header X-API-GATEWAY: true (this bypasses the banner) or we can temporarily disable banner for that org id. But we need to confirm security implications. olivia_engineer: Longer term: gateway should return application/json error payloads when response_format=json or Accept: application/json is present. Also our structured output strict mode should enforce Content-Type on responses and surface a clear 422 or 503 with a JSON error. I'll open an internal issue to change middleware behavior. mike_support: I gave customer the header workaround and asked for their acceptance test. They ran it and said parser now gets JSON again. They asked why we didn't enforce content-type earlier. olivia_engineer: Root cause summary (internal): new gateway banner middleware returned HTML 200 for unknown clients, unaware of structured-output strict enforcement. It didn't respect Accept/response_format headers. We need two fixes: 1) change middleware to return JSON 5xx with content-type application/json for API endpoints when Accept includes application/json; 2) runtime should validate Content-Type before handing response to callers and, if mismatch, return a machine-readable error with request id. lisa_support_mgr: Action items: - olivia_engineer: create PR to update banner middleware to prefer JSON for API requests (ETA: 4h) - raj_sre: patch gateway config to disable banner for acme-242 until PR merges (ETA: 1h) - mike_support: communicate workaround + follow up with customer (ETA: now) - olivia_engineer: add a regression test for structured-output strict mode to assert Content-Type and body parseability (ETA: 48h) mike_support: Customer confirmed workaround works and will accept a temporary disable while we push the fix. I'll update ticket and set high-sev. :thumbsup: olivia_engineer: I'll link the PR here once created. In logs I attached stack snippet showing where parser raised the error: ``` StructuredOutputValidator.parse(responseBody) -> JSON.parse -> SyntaxError: Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0 at validateStructuredOutput (/srv/runtime/validators/json.js:42:15) ``` raj_sre: Noting for postmortem: any middleware that produces non-JSON on API routes must be opt-in. We'll add an integration test on the gateway for Accept header behavior. mike_support: Thanks everyone. I'll close loop with AcmePay after raj patches config. acmepay_integ_bot: (automated) test-run 2026-03-10T02:50Z: header workaround verified, all JSON parsing tests passing. lisa_support_mgr: Good job. Add the incident to postmortems and tag eng-runtime + gateway teams. :eyes:
